bibliographic.title: Is Self-knowledge and Action Consistent or Not: Investigating Large Language Model's Personality
bibliographic.authors: Yiming Ai, Zhiwei He, Ziyin Zhang, Wenhong Zhu, Hongkun Hao, Kai Yu, Lingjun Chen, Rui Wang
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning
bibliographic.citation_apa: Ai, Y., He, Z., Zhang, Z., Zhu, W., Hao, H., Yu, K., Chen, L., & Wang, R. (2024). Is Self-knowledge and Action Consistent or Not: Investigating Large Language Model's Personality. In Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 235).

methodology.method_family: psychometric personality questionnaire assessment and comparison of LLM outputs to human response patterns
methodology.sample_description: LLM outputs examined against observed human response patterns; empirical testing of personality knowledge and behavioral inclinations mentioned but details unclear
methodology.technology_context: Large Language Models assessed via conventional personality questionnaires and real-world behavioral tendencies

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study evaluates LLM personality validity and alignment between self-knowledge and action using psychometric questionnaires; it does not address conversational AI systems, governance mechanisms, oversight, compliance, auditability, or deployment in regulated high-stakes environments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper concerns LLMs and briefly mentions safety and responsibility, its core focus is anthropomorphic personality assessment and the disjunction between stated traits and demonstrated behavior. The provided text contains no evidence on conversational governance, chatbots/agents, guardrails, observability, human oversight, contestation, or regulated-domain operational controls. Python triage flagged it as supporting_candidate, but full-text scope is misaligned with the review's governance focus.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on front matter (pages 1-2 fragment). Objective is clearly stated, but methods, sample, analysis, results, limitations, and ethics are not sufficiently described in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The abstract and introduction are internally coherent about studying self-knowledge versus action in LLMs, but the excerpt provides insufficient methodological detail for strong appraisal. Relevance to conversational governance in regulated settings is very low based on available text.

coding.subtheme: Disjunction between LLM self-knowledge and demonstrated action

synthesis.main_claim: Conventional personality questionnaires may not reliably capture genuine LLM personality inclinations, and LLMs may show a disjunction between personality traits they claim to possess and tendencies demonstrated in real-world scenarios.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces and operationalizes the distinction between self-knowledge and action for LLMs, motivating empirical examination of alignment between questionnaire-based personality claims and behavioral tendencies.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance; at most peripheral foundational context on LLM trait-behavior inconsistency with indirect implications for safety and responsibility.
